title: Series triage with one hERG liability
context: Your medchem team has a congeneric series against the primary target. Enzyme potency is comparable across the four analogues below (all single-digit nM), so the next-compound decision turns on developability, not potency. Synthesis capacity is limited: you can carry at most three forward and must drop at least one. Candidate structures are the four compounds below (SMILES available via their ADMET records).
decision_required: Run ADMET on the series, then recommend which analogues to advance and which single analogue to deprioritize, with its dominant liability. Finish with a DECISION block: advance: <labels> / deprioritize: <labels> / primary_liability: <name>.

C3.note: Terfenadine-like: hERG IC50 0.2 uM — the classic QT/torsades liability that forces the drop; others are hERG-safe with clean DILI/Ames.

source: Ground-truth liabilities from the B1 ADMET gold (ChEMBL/FDA-label measured values); decision is an objective consequence of those values.

title: Series triage with one genotoxic analogue
context: Four analogues from a lead series share acceptable potency and physicochemical profiles. Before committing synthesis for the next DMPK round, you need a go/no-go on each. One analogue carries a hard-stop safety flag the others do not. Compound structures are available via their ADMET records.
decision_required: Run ADMET, then recommend advance/deprioritize and name the dominant liability of the compound you drop. Finish with a DECISION block: advance: <labels> / deprioritize: <labels> / primary_liability: <name>.

C3.note: Thalidomide-like: Ames-positive (genotoxicity) is the single dominant flag; hERG-safe and DILI-negative, so the drop is driven by mutagenicity, not cardiotox or hepatotox.

source: Ground-truth liabilities from the B1 ADMET gold; genotoxicity (Ames) is the decisive hard stop.

title: Multi-parameter trade-off with no clean compound
context: This late-stage series has no liability-free analogue — every candidate shows a moderate hERG signal, and the decision is a genuine trade-off across hERG, hepatotoxicity (DILI), genotoxicity (Ames) and drug-likeness (Ro5). You must pick the best developability profile to advance and drop the one with the worst stacked liability. Structures are available via their ADMET records.
decision_required: Run ADMET, weigh the full multi-parameter profile, then recommend the best analogue(s) to advance and the single analogue to deprioritize with its dominant liability. Finish with a DECISION block: advance: <labels> / deprioritize: <labels> / primary_liability: <name>.

C3.note: Doxorubicin-like: the only analogue stacking genotoxicity (Ames+), hepatotox (DILI+) and a Ro5 failure — worst overall, unambiguous drop.

C1.note: cleanest: highest hERG IC50, no DILI/Ames

source: Ground-truth liabilities from the B1 ADMET gold; the drop is the stacked-liability compound, the advance set is the two with clean DILI/Ames and the widest hERG margins.
